title: EU data-anchor pilot — financial, ops, and customer comms notes
body:
Purpose
-----
Quick working notes for the EU Data-Anchor pilot (short: EU-anchor). This doc collects financial scenarios, operational runbook steps, and customer communication templates for the initial pilot with three customers. Focus is on (a) minimizing customer-visible disruption, (b) clearly tracking incremental cost by tenant, and (c) having an auditable evidence packet for compliance reviewers.

Context and scope
-----------------
- Pilot goal: validate region-anchoring (tenant pinned to EU compute + storage) for a set of mid-market customers who require EU residency.
- Not full productization — this is a staged experiment that will exercise routing, storage anchors, billing tags, and rollback.
- Timeline: 2025-09 (design) -> 2025-10 (lab tests) -> 2025-11 (customer pilot start) -> 2025-01 (evaluate).

Success criteria (binary + measurable)
-------------------------------------
1) Residency: 100% of API requests for pinned tenants route to EU compute and storage (per telemetry) for 30 days.
   - Metric: percent requests with region_tag=europe && storage_host=eu-storage >= 99.9%
2) Cost attribution: per-tenant incremental cost for dedicated anchor tracked in billing system (chargeable tags).
   - Metric: monthly incremental cost per tenant itemized (compute, storage, egress) and visible in billing export.
3) SLA alignment: Latency SLOs remain within 2x baseline for 95th pctiles.
4) Audit evidence: generate customer evidence-bundle (routing logs + config snapshot) on demand within 2 business days.

Operational scenarios modelled in pilot
--------------------------------------
A. Normal steady state (anchored): tenant routed to EU, local KV/cache warm, no failover.
B. Regional outage (EU partial/outage): automated fallback to nearby region (policy-mode: manual-approval for pilot) or queued requests depending on customer policy.
C. Customer requests pin change (move out / move to another territory): manual workflow with data-copy vs re-anchor decision.
D. Billing dispute scenario: customer queries spikes due to anchor cost — need line-item export and operator narrative.

Financial model (work-in-progress)
----------------------------------
- Inputs: per-hour dedicated vGPU cost (e.g., p4x@€5.40/hr), storage gb/mo (€0.12/GB), egress per GB, incremental operator hours.
- Allocation: for pilot we'll amortize shared EU anchor infra across participants using weighted CPU-hours consumed.
- Example quick estimate (per-tenant monthly):
  * Average usage: 20k requests/day, mean tokens/day 1.2M -> deduced GPU-hours: 40h/mo (batching assumed)
  * Compute cost: 40h * €5.4 = €216
  * Storage snapshot + anchors: 200GB * €0.12 = €24
  * Network egress: 150GB * €0.09 = €13.5
  * Ops overhead + monitoring + amortized infra: ~€60
  -> Rough total = €313.5/mo per active pilot tenant (very rough — refine with real telemetry).
- Risk note: if anchors require reserved capacity (Dedicated pools), the marginal cost model changes to committed-monthly buckets — see JIRA: JIRA-EUANCHOR-44 for capex/commitment options.

Billing tags and export fields required
------------------------------------
- tenant_id, anchor_region, anchor_pool_id, cost_center, usage_tokens, gpu_hours, storage_gb, egress_gb, operator_tag
- Export sample path: s3://billing-exports/eu-anchor/2025-11/<tenant>-usage.csv
- Action: Product ops to add these tags to billing CSV exporter (owner: Priya Shah, JIRA-EUANCHOR-102).

Customer communication (templates / snippets)
--------------------------------------------
1) Pre-activation notice (72h)
   Subject: Upcoming EU residency activation for <TenantName>
   Body: We will enable EU residency anchoring for your account on <date>. During activation there may be a brief (~1–3 min) service interruption while routing is updated. If you have specific compliance artifacts required, reply to this thread and we will attach them to your evidence packet.

2) Post-activation evidence packet (on-demand)
   - config snapshot (routing table + anchor_pool_id)
   - sample request logs (24h window) showing request -> eu compute mapping
   - storage location manifest (s3 path prefixes)

3) Outage fallback notice (customer-facing, if fallback triggers)
   Body: On <date/time> we temporarily routed your requests to a fallback region due to an outage affecting EU compute. No customer data left the EU storage anchor; ephemeral compute was temporarily in <region>. We have a full incident report on request.

Operator runbook (pilot-mode, manual steps highlighted)
------------------------------------------------------
Pre-activation checklist (SRE/Oncall)
- Verify tenant consent exists (contract clause present).
- Confirm anchor_pool has capacity & bootstrap images deployed.
- Create evidence-bundle skeleton in /evidence/<tenant>/<activation-date>.
- Tag billing exporter with tenant tags (verify one sample row).
- Smoke test: curl against tenant endpoint with region header -> expect EU endpoint IP and storage prefix.

Activation steps (operators)
1) Create anchor assignment: POST /internal/anchors assign {tenant, anchor_pool_id} (owner: Mateo Alvarez)
2) Push routing policy: feature-flag: tenant.region_pin=EU (rollout via console)
3) Warm caches: run canonical prompt set (script: scripts/warm_eu_anchor.sh <tenant>)
4) Validate telemetry: run query (Elastic): requests | filter tenant_id==X && region==eu | count() -> expect >0 within 30s
5) Notify customer with pre-approved template

Fallback & rollback
- For pilot we will NOT auto-failover across regions for pinned tenants without manual approval. Trigger path: Pager on-call -> SRE lead manual approval -> run rollback script to mark tenant as pinned:fallback->true.
- Evidence requirement when fallback occurs: collect routing logs (t= -30m..+30m), config snapshot, operator approval notes. Attach to customer ticket.

Testing checklist (lab)
- Simulate EU compute outage using chaos runner (tag: eu-zone-sim). Verify manual fallback flow and evidence packet collection.
- Load test anchored tenant at expected tok/day profile; confirm 95th pctl latency <= 2x baseline.
- Validate billing export includes new fields (spot-check sample csv).

Open questions (needs decisions)
- Billing model: per-tenant marginal charge vs percent-of-pool amortization? (Product finance)
- Default fallback policy for pilot: manual vs auto? (SRE + Legal recommend manual)
- Evidence retention period for audits: 90d vs 365d? (Legal)
- When to convert pilot anchors to Dedicated reserved pools (threshold by sustained GPU-hours).

Action items (owners + rough ETA)
- Priya: Add billing tags to exporter + sample CSV by 2025-10-01 (JIRA-EUANCHOR-102).
- Mateo: Provide warmup scripts and activation POST endpoint docs by 2025-09-20 (GH PR: region-routing#312).
- Tom: Run cost-sensitivity analysis for reserved vs on-demand days by 2025-09-25 (JIRA-EUANCHOR-44).
- Elena: Draft customer pre/post templates and evidence packet checklist by 2025-09-15 (confluence: CONFLUENCE-12345).

Notes to self / rough operator tips
- Keep one operator on-call during first 48h of activation windows (timezone overlap EU morning + US evening).
- If telemetry shows >1% requests slipping out of EU after activation, escalate to routing-eng immediately — likely stale edge caches.
- Preserve raw routing logs; derived aggregates are not sufficient for compliance audit.

Appendix: sample commands and telemetry queries
----------------------------------------------
- Warm caches (example): ./scripts/warm_eu_anchor.sh tenant-123 --prompts prompts/eu-anchor-canon.json
- Elastic query (example): POST /_search body: {"query":{"bool":{"filter":[{"term":{"tenant_id":"tenant-123"}},{"term":{"region":"eu"}}]}}} (adjust timeval to last 5m)
- Billing export sample: head s3://billing-exports/eu-anchor/2025-11/tenant-123-usage.csv

End — iterative doc. Keep lean, update with telemetry once we have real token/hour numbers from pilot tenants.
